scenes.narration: Did you know there's a minivan that rockets to 60 in just 4.4 seconds? That's the R63 AMG, a rare breed with only a few hundred ever made.

scenes.headline: Rare AMG Minivan
scenes.narration: This sports tourer features AMG's distinctive five-spoke wheels, underlining its unique performance pedigree.

scenes.headline: Engine
scenes.narration: Power comes from the handcrafted 6.2-liter V8, boasting 503 horsepower and 465 lb-ft of torque. It’s one of AMG’s finest engines, known for its performance in other high-profile models.

scenes.headline: Market Value
scenes.narration: Originally priced around $90,000, they go for about $64,500 today. That's approximately a 4% yearly depreciation rate.

scenes.headline: Interior Features
scenes.narration: Inside, AMG-branded pedals and bespoke seven-passenger seating merge performance with unique luxury. Would you choose this ultimate sleeper for your garage?

script: Did you know there's a minivan that rockets to 60 in just 4.4 seconds? That's the R63 AMG, a rare breed with only a few hundred ever made. This sports tourer features AMG's distinctive five-spoke wheels, underlining its unique performance pedigree. Power comes from the handcrafted 6.2-liter V8, boasting 503 horsepower and 465 lb-ft of torque. It’s one of AMG’s finest engines, known for its performance in other high-profile models. Originally priced around $90,000, they go for about $64,500 today. That's approximately a 4% yearly depreciation rate. Inside, AMG-branded pedals and bespoke seven-passenger seating merge performance with unique luxury. Would you choose this ultimate sleeper for your garage?

sections.Highlights: THIS... is a 2007 Mercedes-Benz R63 AMG, finished in Obsidian Black Metallic with a black interior. The attached Carfax vehicle history report shows no accidents or mileage discrepancies in this R63’s past. According to the Monroney Label provided in the gallery, notable factory equipment includes Airmatic adaptive air suspension, a panoramic sunroof, third-row seats, Distronic adaptive cruise control, and a Harman/Kardon sound system. Notable modifications reported by the seller are limited to 20-inch AMG 5-spoke wheels. One of the more unexpected products of Mercedes-Benz's range expansion during the 2000s was the W251 R-Class. It was eloquently called a "Sports Tourer" by Mercedes-Benz, but was a minivan in every aspect other than its lack of the sliding rear doors common in its segment. The extremely rare R63 AMG model featured the powerful 6.2-liter V8 that propelled the vehicle to 60 miles per hour in approximately 4.4 seconds, making it the fastest production minivan in the world. Production began in the United States in 2006 and ended after the 2013 model year. Power comes from an M156 6.2-liter V8, rated at 503 horsepower and 465 lb-ft of torque. Output is sent to all four wheels via a 7-speed automatic transmission and Mercedes-Benz's 4Matic permanent all-wheel drive system.
sections.Equipment: A Monroney Label is provided in the photo gallery, and a partial list of notable equipment reported by the seller includes: Lighting Package (bi-xenon headlights with curve illumination, headlight washers, corner illuminating front foglamps) Airmatic adaptive air suspension system Panoramic sunroof Third-row seats Keyless Go Distronic adaptive cruise control Harman/Kardon sound system
sections.Seller Notes: The attached Carfax history report indicates an ownership change in March 2023. The seller reports that this is a clerical error, and they have filed a dispute claim with Carfax. The seller notes that the May 2025 service record erroneously indicates a mileage of 1,060 miles.
